testcase.name: A: clamp always returns a value inside its bounds (or the lower bound for NaN); infinite bounds are allowed
B: axisAngle accepts any finite angle and any finite axis whose largest component is at least 1e-12 (Tier 3 validation only)
B: Pose.toLocal with scale 1e-100 and world components at 1e100 is finite (domain edge)
B: slerp and nlerp are accurate for finite unit quaternions and |t| up to 1e3 (extrapolation included)
A: approxEquals is false when the difference is NaN (equal infinities) and never throws
B: Quat.mul and Quat.dot are finite for components up to 1e100 (not only unit quaternions)
B: Vec3.mul(s) and Vec3.lerp(to, t) are finite for components and scalars up to 1e100; outside that, IEEE
A: finiteness and unit length of the fallback path belong to the caller
A: normalizedOr returns the caller's fallback object unchanged, even when it is NaN, infinite, zero or not unit
